data.name: Requiescence
data.detailed_description:
Overview:


It's been a year of hard travel, but finally, the young mage Kymil arrives at his destination.

He's a Cyromancer - a spellcaster who wields the power of ice to smite down his enemies. Kymil learned how to harness his power thanks to his uncle, a well-renowned adventurer who hunted down treasure on every corner of the continent.

But his uncle was murdered in his home by an unknown assailant, and Kymil is driven to uncover the mystery behind his death. The only clue he has is an unfinished entry in his uncle's notes about a mysterious cathedral in the middle of the sprawling Dead Plains...

When he arrives at the cathedral, Kymil has no idea what he's searching for or where to go. But something in him presses him forward, and he's determined to figure out the cathedral's secrets, no matter how dire the cost.

Features:


  • 125,000 word novel -- 10-15 hours of gameplay!
  • Unique hybrid of Western and Anime-style art -- 17 CGs and 13 Characters with unique expressions!
  • Interactivity -- 3 different romance routes with 6 total endings!
  • Partial English voice acting!
  • Full original soundtrack -- 13 tracks total

About:


Requiescence is a visual novel - a 2D narrative-based game that presents the user with important choices to alter the story's path. Primarily a story of action and adventure, Requiescence features three prominent romance routes that significantly change the later portions of the game.

The game is also a BL (boy's love) game, which means both the main character and the love interests are male.

If you're familiar with Nitro+CHiRAL games (Togainu no Chi, Lamento, DRAMAtical Murder, Sweet Pool), then you know how amazing a story can become when you mingle an epic adventure with intricate character relationships. Requiescence is heavily inspired by these games and aims for a similar style, while still putting a fresh twist on the BL genre.

reviews.review:
"Requiescence" is a BL visual novel, so obviously it needed to find itself in my Steam library, sooner or later. It looked like something I would enjoy, because of fantasy setting, detailed lore and a bit darker tone. Now, after finishing all routes and getting all endings (it took me about 10 hours) I can say, I'm satisfied with this purchase.

[h1]Good things:[/h1]

[b] Easily accessible +18 version.[/b] Obviously developer couldn't put full version of the game here, but every Steam purchase comes with download link, where you can find it. Maybe it shouldn't be surprising, but still deserves a praise, when so many developers refuse to patch their games on Steam or even try to make more money, by forcing players to buy "content restoration" DLCs or full games from other sites. Huge plus for the Argent Games.

[b] Music/sounds.[/b] Music in this game is amazing. Quite a few visual novels developers should learn from "Requiescence" how to reflect every scene with fitting soundtrack. Sounds can get a bit repetitive, but they add great amount of immersion to the game. It's also worth mentioning that this game has a voice acting, not a bad one, from what I've heard, but I've turned it out very quickly (I'll explain why below), so can't say much more about it.

[b] Atmosphere.[/b] "Requiescence" does a great job at creating dark, gloomy atmosphere. When I was playing it for the first time, on some occasions, music itself was enough to give me creeps.

[b] Writing.[/b] I would say that writing is probably the best part of the game. It's solid, engaging, descriptive, dialogues looks well and realistic. Some phrases are a bit overused (there is way too much tongue clicking and eyes rolling for example), but that's my only complaint in that regard.

[b] Characters.[/b] I was hesitant to add it under "good things", because I'm a little conflicted. As much as I've enjoyed protagonist and three main characters, I felt that secondary characters were completely bland and bad guys... Well, they were bad guys. There's no much depth to them or their actions, game didn't make an effort to make me dislike them or be afraid of them, or understand their motives, or presents them in interesting way. That being said, three pursuable characters were unique, had a little bit of backstory, that explained their actions and I end up liking every single one of them.

[b] Protagonist.[/b] BL protagonists have the same set of flaws that otome protagonists struggle with. They are usually very naive, soft-spoken, innocent, they often presents amazing levels of stupidity and have less personality than a toast. Kymil wasn't like that. He was an interesting protagonist, definitely passive in comparison to his love options [spoiler]classic uke character - no variation here[/spoiler] and rather delicate, but it was realistic, he didn't seem hopeless, he stand for what he believed in and I liked him.

[b]Price.[/b] Amount of content is worth the price.

[h1]Minor complaints:[/h1]

[b] Endings.[/b] That will be completely subjective, but good endings are a bit bland and not much satisfying, while bad endings are classic yaoi bad ends. In short, [spoiler] you end up being someone's sex toy. Every. God. Damn. Time.[/spoiler] Honestly I've expected a little more creative approach, but I know some people will enjoy it. [i]Small edit: [/i]I would like to express myself better. I feel like bad endings could work in the form they are, if they were established better. [Spoiler] If demon on Damian's route would be more manipulative and gained MC trust or the contrary, would go full creep and do some nasty stuff while it lasted, ending would have much more "power" to it, as we, as players, would know character a bit better. Same goes for Absalom. It's completely out of character for Kymil to pick him and go go along with his proposition. If Absalom would be more present on Kaul's route, I may start to think which one I like better, which one is right. I had this sort of thoughts between Absalom and the Monk, the issue is, Kymil isn't choosing between those two, but between Absalom and his loved one, which is much better established character, has a personality, understandable goals and all that. And the Monk's ending... Well, let's just say, it was the most "out of the blue" and didn't quite make sense. [/spoiler]

[b] Graphic.[/b] "Requiescence" falls the most in terms of visuals. It's not a big deal regarding relatively low price, but it's worth poiting out. Character models looks well, but were way too similar to each other in terms of faces and body types. [Spoiler]When I saw Absalom for the first time, I thought it was Carrault. In wig. Seriously.[/spoiler] There is low number of CGs and they don't look the best either - especially faces, on some CGs they look very weird. Backgrounds are bland and most of them looks like photos with filter over them, which is, most likely, what they are.

[b] Voice acting doesn't always match what is written.[/b] And that is fine, in game's description there is information of partial voice acting, but I don't think I've ever seen game voiced in... that way. Partial voice acting usually means the characters have some sort of phrases or speak during cut-scenes, or something like that, here a lot of dialogues were voiced and a lot of weren't, without any sense or pattern. It was breaking the immersion. It was frustrating and confusing. Also, for the future, it would be good to have option not to turn all the voices at once, but every single one of them separately. Personally I don't like voiced MC and there's always a possibility that some voice will seem annoying to someone. It's a minor tweak, but worth implementing.

[b]A little more one-on-one scenes would be nice.[/b] And I don't mean THAT kind of scenes. As it often happens in visual novels, characters seem weirdly and way too soon drawn to protagonist. The mutual feelings didn't seem very natural.

Despite small flaws, I can recommend "Requiescence" to every BL fan out there.
